audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[].side reads 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] and the packet levelChart both read Ekko on all seven.
audit.why: Brand has no dash, no blink and no escape in the kit; Sear only stuns a target already ablaze, so a clean Ekko can step in and out of a stun that cannot fire. 54.29% over 1048 games agrees.
audit.corrected: All seven full-layer rows moved to Ekko with whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text names 'Everfrost or your burst item' — a vague item clause that does not match the itemization the same page recommends (Rocketbelt/Stormsurge).
audit.why: Placeholder item phrasing; name the actual item or drop the clause.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Hextech Rocketbelt, the first item report[8] actually recommends, and the level 6 spike now carries the 110s Chronobreak against his 100s Pyroclasm.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is stated only obliquely: Sear stuns ONLY if the target is already ablaze from Blaze, so the ability that actually beats you is whichever of Pillar of Flame or Conflagration lands first.
audit.why: Riot's text for Sear: it stuns only 'If the target is ablaze'. Blaze comes from any of his spells landing. That inverts the dodge priority the page currently teaches.
audit.corrected: cooldowns, enemyWin, report[5].t and phases[0].why now say to avoid taking the Blaze stack, not to dodge the stun itself.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that must hold real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Now carries Sear 8s, Pillar of Flame 10s, Conflagration 13s, Pyroclasm 100s, Chronobreak 110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2).
audit.why: Bodies did not match their titles.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten to their own titles using Brand's 10s/13s gap and Ekko's 110s R.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Q both passes, then step off — with no Blaze stack on you his Sear cannot stun, it can only sting.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: E blink-strike window opens: Q-E-auto is your first real trade and the third passive hit stings already.
edits.after: E opens the blink-strike: Q, E the gap, auto for the third passive hit, and leave before Blaze stacks up.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: W zone games begin: drop it on his retreat line BEFORE trading and the stun finds him mid-regret.
edits.after: Drop W on his retreat line before you trade — he owns no dash, so the stun lands exactly where you put it.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: Three-hit trades on cooldown — Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk. Bank the tempo for 6.
edits.after: Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk — his Sear is 8s and he owns nothing to disengage with.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: Chronobreak online — your aggression gets a save file. Trade like the rewind exists, because it does.
edits.after: Chronobreak at 110s rewinds you out of a landed Pyroclasm — his 100s ultimate stops closing kills.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: First item spike: the full string deletes half bars and the rewind erases the counter-argument.
edits.after: First item: the string deletes half his bar and, with zero mobility, he has to eat every hit of it.

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Ekko

edits.before: Late Ekko picks and survives: dive their carry, W the peel, and Chronobreak out of whatever they answered with.
edits.after: Late he is a stationary poke turret — flank him, dive, and Chronobreak out before his team can peel.

edits.before: - Brand Sear (Stun): matchup-defining — Q only stuns when you are ablaze — after eating W or E, the stun line is the dodge that matters. Check it before every step-up. - R Chronobreak is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Sear is 8s at rank 1 and only stuns a target already ablaze — stay clean of Blaze and his stun is just a ball of fire. - Pillar of Flame is 10s and Conflagration 13s: that gap is your entry. - Pyroclasm is 100s; your 110s Chronobreak answers it.

edits.before: Brand wins by landing Sear (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Brand wins by chipping a Blaze stack onto you first, stunning with Sear, and detonating the whole rotation.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry by punishing immobility — he owns no dash and no escape, so every string you open on him he must finish.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Conflagration is 13s and Pillar of Flame 10s — step in when both are spent and he is left with a Sear that cannot stun.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 — under half health without it, one Blaze detonation plus Sear finishes you.

edits.before: Track Brand’s Sear (Stun): Q only stuns when you are ablaze — after eating W or E, the stun line is the dodge that matters. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Sear (8s): it stuns only if Blaze is already burning on you, so the spell that actually kills you is the W or E that lands first — dodge that one.

edits.before: You out-scale him hard once Everfrost or your burst item lands — Brand's damage is real but immobile, and you can dive him before he lands his full combo.
edits.after: You out-scale him once Hextech Rocketbelt lands — Brand's damage is real but he has no dash, so you can dive him before Blaze stacks and Sear can stun.

notes: Content win[] already read Ekko on all seven rows and matches the packet levelChart; only the full-layer sides were stuck on 'Skill', so the side edits bring full into agreement with content and no paired win[N] edit exists to propose. spikes[2] previously named Everfrost, which does not match the itemization the same page recommends — replaced with Hextech Rocketbelt from report[8]. Whether Chronobreak's untargetable window drops an in-flight Pyroclasm bounce entirely, as spikes[1] claims, is not stated in Riot's text; left that line alone rather than sharpen a claim I cannot verify.
